title: Discussion: Prototyping Generative AI Applications
html:
This discussion area is an additional means to interact with the weekly discussion and interactions. Please feel free to discuss our weekly topic live during the class session, via teams during the session, and/or here at any time during the week.

Additionally, groups can choose to present their weekly homework topics here if they choose to do so.

  1. Before the first meeting of the week:
    • Provide a substantive post reflecting on the reading materials and slide deck:
      1. One concept that was interesting to you and how you can apply it to your future career or life.
      2. One concept that was difficult to understand and what made it confusing.
      3. One external resource you found that helped you understand the concept better, along with an explanation of how it helped.
    • (Optional) Contribute to the group aspect of the weekly assignment.
  2. After the first meeting and before the second meeting of the week:
    • View and respond to the course recording.
    • Provide a written version of the in-class activities prior to the second meeting of the week AND
    • Respond to at least one peer to continue the conversation, clarify an idea, or share a relevant resource (you can respond to live session discussion points or online posts).
  3. Complete the weekly assignment.

Weekly Discussion Prompts: Prototyping Generative AI Applications

Use the prompts below to anchor your initial post, guide group collaboration, or prepare your responses:

Prompt 1: Rapid Prototyping with Streamlit vs. Production Frontend Stacks

  • Context: Streamlit and Gradio allow AI developers to build interactive, stateful web applications directly in Python in an afternoon. However, production enterprise applications often require robust frontend architectures (React, Next.js, mobile clients).
  • Discussion Question: What is the strategic value of rapid Python-based prototyping during early product validation? At what point in an application's lifecycle should a team transition from a Streamlit prototype to a decoupled microservice API and custom frontend?

Prompt 2: The Critical Role of Chunking and Vector Retrieval

  • Context: In RAG pipelines, retrieval quality depends heavily on chunking strategy (fixed-character, recursive paragraph, semantic sentence clustering). If chunks are too small, context is lost; if too large, vector similarity matches degrade.
  • Discussion Question: Describe how you would design the chunking and embedding pipeline for complex technical documentation (with code snippets, tables, and prose). How does cross-encoder re-ranking help surface the most relevant chunk?

Prompt 3: User Experience: Latency, Streaming, and Cost Management

  • Context: Generative AI applications have fundamentally different latency profiles than traditional CRUD apps. While traditional databases respond in milliseconds, an LLM generating 500 tokens can take several seconds.
  • Discussion Question: Why is token streaming (Server-Sent Events / WebSockets) essential for user retention in AI apps? What caching strategies (semantic caching, prompt caching) can minimize latency and API expenses?

Prompt 4: Group Homework Topic Presentations (Optional)

  • If your group is choosing to present your weekly assignment findings here on the board, please share your slide link, code/workflow summary, and a brief overview of the problem you solved. Group members must reply within the thread to document individual contributions.
